E1 states that a Cr2O3 barrier is absent and offers no protection, implying Fe-oxides alone are insufficient. E2 describes a complex CoNiV alloy with a specific oxide barrier film, which is not relevant to Fe-oxides on Q235 steel. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: A pre-formed Fe-oxide layer on Q235 steel can be coherent and adherent
Such an oxide layer acts as a physical barrier to chloride ions and oxygen
Reduced ingress of Cl- and O2 lowers the electrochemical driving force for iron dissolution
This barrier effect delays localized corrosion like pitting
The cited evidence supports the barrier mechanism for Fe-oxides on steel
